title: The pure-tensor-normalized signed Koszul completion model
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $A$ a commutative ring and $\rho:A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ a ring map. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their global-section Hom action [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module], cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and the total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and rank-one scalar map of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. For $a:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, including $r=0$, define $Q_{m+1}$ as the ordered tensor of $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\rho(a_i)^{m+1}}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with the empty tensor $\mathcal O[0]$, and $T_m(K)=K\otimes Q_{m+1}$. A signed completion model consists of finite-coordinate isomorphisms $T_m(K)^q\cong\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}K^{q+|I|}$, normalized so the inclusion of $z$ in summand $I$ is exactly $z\otimes e_I$, where every entry of $e_I$ is one, its degree is $-1$ precisely at the indices in $I$, and all inclusions use the total-tensor inclusions and inverse unitors in the same factor order. In these coordinates the differential on $z e_I$, $p=q+|I|$, is $(d_Kz)e_I+\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^p(-1)^{|\{j\in I:j<i\}|}a_i^{m+1}z e_{I\setminus\{i\}}$; coefficient chain maps are diagonal. The model has natural inverse transitions $T_{m+1}\to T_m$, diagonal on $I$ with scalar $\prod_{i\in I}a_i$, and natural inclusions $K\to T_m(K)$ given by the empty coordinate. It has a functor $B$, natural projections exhibiting $B(K)$ as the product [def-weil-category-product] of all $T_m(K)$ in complexes, a natural shift $s$ with $\operatorname{pr}_m s=t_m\operatorname{pr}_{m+1}$, and the natural diagonal $e:K\to B(K)$ with these inclusions as projections. Finally it has a functor $H$ with specified degreewise binary-biproduct coordinates $H(K)^q\cong B(K)^q\oplus B(K)^{q-1}$, differential $(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, diagonal action on chain maps, and natural unit $\eta_K=(e_K,0)$. This is a structure of completely specified coordinates and universal properties; it does not choose an object from a bare existence theorem. The generic coordinate structure accepts an explicitly supplied Hom-scalar operation; the ringed specialization uses precisely the action induced by $\rho$.
